public_source_audit.source: Godin & Thivierge, PLOS Computational Biology 2026, DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719, published 2026-08-25
observations: Live PLOS article states SPLiT uses online Oja tracking of a k-dimensional empirical activity subspace plus normalized LMS in manifold coordinates.
The paper states Oja tracking assumes manifold drift is slow relative to the tracking update and that the subspace estimate is re-orthonormalized every time step.

The paper explicitly acknowledges that low-dimensional projections or regularized variants of full-space learning can mitigate conditioning issues, so Oja-specific benefit must be separated from the generic value of adaptive subspace restriction.

S1 Code remains linked as Code.zip (DOI 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1014719.s002), but read-only file-level recovery remained blocked in this invocation; no source-exact S8/S11/S12 reproduction was performed.
public_source_audit.scope: Paper inspection plus bounded source-derived synthetic controls; not an exact reproduction of the authors' recurrent network, Oja implementation, or supporting code.

bounded_audit.status: online rank-selection and dormant-subspace-memory boundary test; non-reproduction

design.ambient_drift: true 72-degree rotation between orthogonal 3D endpoint subspaces
design.structured_factor: fixed ambient direction orthogonal to endpoint base manifolds; amplitude a
design.target: normalized linear readout of the 3D latent state plus gamma times structured factor
design.observation_noise: isotropic Gaussian with total RMS sigma 0.25
design.generic_tracker: exponentially weighted covariance PCA, rho=0.985, top-4 basis, eigen update every 5 steps
design.oja_like_tracker: bounded source-derived stochastic subspace-Oja update, eta=0.2, with small within-subspace covariance rotation; not source-exact SPLiT
design.decoders: RLS in tracked coordinates; full ambient RLS control
design.rank_selector: prequential-loss hysteresis: run k=3 and k=4 intrinsic RLS experts in parallel and switch only after persistent >=8% EW pre-update loss advantage
design.memory_tracker: on a prolonged effective-rank drop, keep current top-3 observed directions but retain the least-represented direction from the previous 4D subspace as a dormant memory; resume ordinary top-4 PCA after spectral recovery
design.memory_detector: k3/k2 eigenvalue ratio; on<0.25, off>0.40, persistence=3 PCA updates. Thresholds chosen from a separate diagnostic seed, then evaluated on disjoint held-out seeds.

rank_selection_results.interpretation: Task-aware k=3↔4 switching did not beat the best fixed-rank intrinsic model in these held-out conditions. It correctly moved to k=4 when the fourth factor was predictive, but switch cost and tracker error remained. Under prolonged temporary rank collapse, selecting rank alone did not preserve a latent direction that disappeared from the covariance.

tracker_specificity_result.interpretation: The generic EW-PCA tracker was materially better than the bounded Oja-like tracker in stable useful/nuisance-fourth scenarios under the same rank-selection rule. This provides no evidence for Oja specificity; however the Oja-like implementation is not source-exact and therefore cannot be used as negative evidence against SPLiT's published Oja implementation.

bounded_audit.interpretation: A simple dormant-subspace memory did not materially help short 25% collapse, but it removed most of the failure from 40% collapse and was essentially neutral without collapse. Immediately after a long collapse it still lagged full ambient RLS, but it prevented the severe post-collapse error spike of ordinary top-4 tracking and later recovered to lower error than the ordinary tracker. This isolates a new boundary: when a task-relevant latent mode becomes temporarily silent, preserving a memory of the inactive subspace can matter more than choosing k online.

limits: All controls are synthetic linear-latent streams and are not source-exact SPLiT/Oja recurrent dynamics.
The memory detector uses hand-specified spectral hysteresis thresholds selected from one diagnostic seed; it is a proof-of-principle, not an optimized or biologically established mechanism.
The generic EW-PCA tracker uses O(N^2) covariance state and is not a biological/scalable substitute for Oja; its role is a causal control for tracker quality.
Parallel k=3/k=4 prequential experts double small decoder state and should not be interpreted as a minimal implementation.
The 40% collapse result should not be generalized to arbitrary covariance degeneracy, nonlinear manifolds, or real neural data.

candidate_update.positive_scope: Adaptive low-dimensional tracking can outperform full ambient RLS when the tracked subspace captures task-relevant factors and ambient nuisance/sample limitation dominates. In the bounded control, a dormant-subspace memory sharply reduced recovery failure after prolonged temporary loss of one latent mode.
candidate_update.negative_boundary: Online 3↔4 rank selection alone did not beat the best fixed-rank intrinsic model and did not solve prolonged rank-collapse recovery. Generic EW-PCA outperformed a bounded Oja-like tracker under matched rank-selection, so no Oja-specific advantage is established. Source-exact SPLiT code remains unavailable to this run.

exact_next_action: Retry read-only S1 Code recovery. If still blocked, test whether dormant-subspace memory survives harder conditions: unknown collapse onset, multiple disappearing/reappearing modes, nonlinear/task-switching relevance, and a task-aware criterion that decides whether a newly high-variance direction is useful before expanding rank. Replace the O(N^2) covariance control with O(Nk) generic trackers (PAST/GROUSE-like) and add the same memory mechanism to an Oja-like tracker. Keep all conclusions bounded until source-exact S8/S11/S12 code is recovered.
